feed.title: PHP2Shell — timeline (EN)
feed.subtitle: Live timeline of PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/109619), a critical PHP core RCE (CVSS 9.2). Fixed in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35. Every fact sourced.

entry.title: Calif: “Let’s set the record straight” — dispute over who found it first
entry.summary: Calif stresses that @lcfr_hax was first to discover php2shell and build a working exploit (hash posted 5 Aug), and that his work convinced the PHP Foundation to fix the whole bug class. A response to the Wiz and OpenAI framing of independent discoveries.
entry.content:
Calif stresses that @lcfr_hax was first to discover php2shell and build a working exploit (hash posted 5 Aug), and that his work convinced the PHP Foundation to fix the whole bug class. A response to the Wiz and OpenAI framing of independent discoveries.

Source: @calif_io na X · confirmed · minor

entry.title: The Record: watchTowr sees exploitation attempts, none successful yet
entry.summary: Jake Knott (watchTowr) tells The Record they observe in-the-wild exploitation attempts with various AI-vibecoded PoC tools; nobody has succeeded so far, but that is not expected to last. The piece lists warnings from the EU, Germany, Japan, Australia, the UK and the Netherlands and services taken offline by Nintendo and others. Detectify: roughly half of PHP sites run versions that get no patch.

entry.title: OpenAI: “Patch the Planet” — we led a coalition for two months
entry.summary: OpenAI says it led a coalition of maintainers, researchers and security providers for two months. Calif found a critical flaw using GPT‑5.6 Sol under the Patch the Planet initiative; Wiz independently reported both bugs. OpenAI engaged the US government (White House Super Intelligence Force, ONCD, CISA) and international partners, announces a PHP version checker, a Codex skill and USD 1 billion in subsidised Daybreak access for defenders. It proposes a five-stage coordination framework and openly asks about disclosure windows and whether governments should use a vulnerability to patch systems.

entry.title: Cloudflare: WAF rules in the works since early October, attacks and bypass attempts
entry.summary: According to Cloudflare’s blog, protections were developed from early October and enabled by default on all plans from 21 Oct 03:02 UTC. Cloudflare says that after the leak it saw attack traffic against customers and attackers mutating payloads to bypass the rules. First use of its new “full transaction detection” (request plus response).

entry.title: Calif publishes the full technical write-up and its own timeline
entry.summary: Ryan Austin (Calif): first RCE paths found on 1 Aug, a hash of one finding posted on X on 5 Aug, first report to PHP on 11 Aug, PoC on 14 Aug, confirmed by PHP on 15 Aug, second bug reported on 21 Aug. Root cause (in line with the advisories): an out-of-memory error interrupts request processing halfway and internal state survives pointing into freed memory. Calif traces the story back to Stefan Esser’s 2004 bug, report #78876 from 2020 and the 2024 OSTIF/Quarkslab audit.
entry.content:
Ryan Austin (Calif): first RCE paths found on 1 Aug, a hash of one finding posted on X on 5 Aug, first report to PHP on 11 Aug, PoC on 14 Aug, confirmed by PHP on 15 Aug, second bug reported on 21 Aug. Root cause (in line with the advisories): an out-of-memory error interrupts request processing halfway and internal state survives pointing into freed memory. Calif traces the story back to Stefan Esser’s 2004 bug, report #78876 from 2020 and the 2024 OSTIF/Quarkslab audit.

Source: Calif — php2shell: A tale of two PHP remote vulnerabilities · confirmed · major
